data.name: Portugal
data.summary: Residents pay a flat 28% on capital gains and dividends (35% if from blacklisted jurisdictions); since 2024, 10%/20%/30% of gains on listed securities and fund units held 2/5/8+ years is excluded (effective 19.6% after 8 years). Children, spouse and parents are exempt from the 10% stamp duty on inheritances and gifts; only a 0.8% stamp duty on gifts of Portuguese real estate remains. No general wealth tax, but AIMI (from 0.7%) on Portuguese real estate above EUR 600,000 per person. The IFICI regime ('NHR 2.0') exempts most foreign income but only for people working in qualifying high-value activities: it does not help a purely passive investor, and the old NHR is closed to new arrivals.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: Worldwide taxation. Investment income and gains taxed at special flat rates (28%), with an option to aggregate at progressive rates (12.5%-48% plus 2.5%/5% solidarity surcharge above EUR 80,000/250,000).
regimes.eligibility: More than 183 days in Portugal in any 12-month period starting or ending in the year, or a habitual residence in Portugal intended as the primary home.

capital_gains.summary: Flat 28% on gains from shares and other securities. Since 2024, gains on listed securities and fund units are partly excluded: 10% if held 2-5 years, 20% if 5-8 years, 30% if 8 years or more. Securities held under 365 days must be aggregated at progressive rates if taxable income (including them) is at least EUR 86,634. Only 50% of gains on unlisted micro/small company shares is taxed. 35% for blacklisted jurisdictions. Real estate: 50% of the gain added to income at progressive rates (up to 48% plus solidarity surcharge); main-home reinvestment relief.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Holding-period exclusions 10%/20%/30% for listed securities and fund units. 50% inclusion for real estate gains and for unlisted micro/small company shares.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Decree-Law 97/2026: gains on residential property sold 2026-2029 exempt if reinvested in Portuguese residential letting at rents up to EUR 2,300/month (conditions).

open_questions: Exact scope of the holding-period exclusion (whether it applies to all listed securities including foreign-listed shares, and its start date) only from PwC's brief mention; statute (CIRS art. 43) not opened.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Listed securities held 8+ years: 28% x 70% = 19.6%. Private company (not micro/small): 28%. Real estate: 50% inclusion x (48% + 5% solidarity surcharge) = 26.5%.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Gains are category G income at 28% regardless of frequency; short-term (<365 days) gains are aggregated at progressive rates for high earners. Professional activity could be category B (business) income.
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: <365 days: compulsory aggregation for high earners. 2/5/8 years: 10/20/30% exclusion on listed securities.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Worldwide gains taxed; credit for foreign tax.

dividends.summary: Flat 28% on dividends (domestic and foreign), or optional aggregation at progressive rates. 35% on investment income from blacklisted jurisdictions. Foreign tax is credited up to the lower of foreign tax, Portuguese tax and the treaty rate.

dividends.withholding_outbound: 28% on dividends to non-residents (treaty reductions; Parent-Subsidiary exemption). Not verified in a source opened.
dividends.treaty_network: About 80 treaties including the US (count not verified).
dividends.holding_company_notes: No holding structure is scored for Portugal: a company that only manages securities or other assets and is majority-owned by one family (or has five or fewer shareholders) is a 'sociedade de simples administração de bens' and is tax-transparent under art. 6 CIRC, so its profit is attributed to the shareholders and taxed as their own income each year; it cannot defer tax, and the participation exemption needs at least a 10% stake.

wealth_tax.summary: No net wealth tax. AIMI (adicional ao IMI) is an annual levy on the total tax-registered value of Portuguese residential/urban land held by an individual: 0.7% above a EUR 600,000 allowance (1% and 1.5% on higher tiers). Foreign assets and financial assets are not taxed.

open_questions: PwC confirms only the 0.7% individual AIMI rate; the EUR 600,000 allowance (doubled for jointly taxed couples) and the 1% (over EUR 1M) / 1.5% (over EUR 2M) tiers are from general knowledge (CIMI art. 135-A ff.).

components.name: AIMI (additional property tax)
components.notes: Base: tax-registered (VPT) value of urban residential property and building land; commercial/services property excluded. Allowance EUR 600,000 per person (EUR 1.2M jointly). Tiers above 0.7% unverified.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: IMI municipal property tax 0.3%-0.45% of registered value (urban). IMT transfer tax up to 7.5% (residential) plus 0.8% stamp duty on purchases.

inheritance.summary: No inheritance tax as such; free transfers (inheritances and gifts) bear 10% stamp duty (verba 1.2 Tabela Geral), but spouses/de facto partners, descendants and ascendants are exempt (Stamp Duty Code art. 6(1)(e)). Gifts of Portuguese real estate still bear 0.8% stamp duty (verba 1.1). Only assets located in Portugal are in scope.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: Children fully exempt from the 10% charge.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Gifts of cash to children should be documented/declared to keep the exemption (not verified).

regimes.name: IFICI ('NHR 2.0', scientific research and innovation incentive)
regimes.description: 10-year regime: 20% flat rate on Portuguese employment/business income from eligible high-value activities, and exemption of most foreign-source income (including dividends, interest and capital gains) except pensions and income from blacklisted jurisdictions. Requires carrying out an eligible activity in an eligible entity: a purely passive investor or family-office principal without such a role does not qualify. The old NHR is closed to people becoming resident after 2024.
regimes.eligibility: Become Portuguese tax resident; not resident in the previous 5 years; never benefited from NHR; carry out an eligible activity (e.g. qualified roles in startups, R&D, certain industrial/export companies, university teaching) in an eligible entity. Apply by 15 January of the year after becoming resident.

capital_gains.summary: Foreign-source capital gains generally exempt (except from blacklisted jurisdictions) for qualifying individuals; Portuguese gains as standard.

income.name: Portugal

income_tax.summary: Resident income tax is progressive from 12.5% to 48% on taxable income, plus a solidarity surcharge of 2.5% above EUR 80,000 and 5% above EUR 250,000, which gives top marginal rates of 50.5% (EUR 86,634 to 250,000) and 53%. Employees pay 11% social security with no stated cap. Self-employed pay 21.4% on a base of 70% of service income (effective 14.98% of income).
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Statutory rate 21.4% on a monthly base equal to one third of the relevant quarterly income, which is 70% of service income (20% of sales); so the recorded effective rate on service income is 21.4% x 70% = 14.98%. The base is capped at 12 times the IAS; with an IAS of EUR 537.13 (the minimum base figure on the PwC page) that is a monthly base of EUR 6,445.56, reached at about EUR 110,495 of annual service income (derived: the 2026 IAS value itself was not found on an official page; EUR 537.13 is the PwC minimum base). Simplified regime (revenue below EUR 200,000): 75% of listed service income is taxed (35% for unlisted services), with a minimum-expense add-back of up to 15% of gross income (EUR 4,587.09 or social security if higher).
income_tax.local_tax_note: No municipal income tax. The specific employment deduction and personal tax credits are not modelled, so personal_allowance is 0.

regimes.name: D8 digital nomad visa
regimes.description: Residence visa for non-EU remote workers earning at least four times the Portuguese minimum wage (official consular page: average monthly income over the last three months of at least four times the monthly minimum guaranteed remuneration; EUR 920 x 4 = EUR 3,680 in 2026, minimum wage per PwC), with income from active work outside Portugal. The first residence permit lasts two years, renewals three years. Holders become tax residents and pay normal IRS (freelancers can use the simplified regime); the visa itself gives no tax relief, though IFICI may be available depending on the activity.
regimes.duration_note: 2-year first permit then 3-year renewals; permanent residence possible after five years.

open_questions: Income threshold (4x minimum wage, 3-month average, annualised to EUR 44,160) confirmed on the consular page vistos.mne.gov.pt; that page does not state the permit duration. The 2-year then 3-year renewal pattern rests on secondary sources.
Social security is owed unless a certificate of coverage applies.

regimes.name: IFICI (NHR 2.0)
regimes.description: Flat 20% on Portuguese-source employment and self-employment income from eligible activities for ten years, with most foreign-source income exempt (pensions excluded). Requires tax residence in Portugal, no residence in the previous five years, no prior NHR, and an eligible activity in an eligible entity: higher-education research, certified start-ups, R&D centres, listed highly qualified professions (a PhD or a degree plus three years of experience), exporting companies (50% of turnover exported) or investment-contract beneficiaries. Remote work for a foreign employer does not qualify by itself. Apply by 15 January of the following year. PwC confirms: residents in the year with no Portuguese residence in the previous five years and no prior NHR, 20% on category A and B income from eligible activities in eligible entities, ten years, foreign-source income exempt except pensions and blacklisted-country income, apply by 15 January of the following year.

income.residence_routes: EU/EEA/Swiss citizens register as residents after three months. US and other non-EU remote workers use the D8 visa (EUR 3,680 a month of active income in 2026, 2-year permit then 3-year renewals); skilled employees need a work visa or a job-seeker route, which was not researched, and the EU Blue Card exists. IFICI is a tax regime open to any new resident with an eligible activity, regardless of nationality.
